items.title: Section: The Perfume Left in an Emptied Bottle — Closing the Five Aspects of Affliction Defilement

items.zh: 漏，若定、若起、若生，於一切時若遇生緣，便現在前。復次，略有二種麁重。一、漏麁重，二、有漏麁重。漏麁重者，阿羅漢等修道所斷煩惱斷時，皆悉永離。此謂有隨眠者有識身中不安隱性、無堪能性。有漏麁重者，隨眠斷時，從漏所生漏所熏發本所得性、不安隱性、苦依附性、與彼相似無堪能性，皆得微薄。又此有漏麁重名煩惱習，阿羅漢、獨覺所未能斷，唯有如來能究竟斷，是故說彼名永斷習氣不共佛法。是名煩惱雜染由五種相差別建立。
items.en: Outflow-coarse-heaviness is entirely and permanently overcome when an arhat or the like exhausts the afflictions severed by the path of cultivation. This refers to the unsettledness and incapacity, within one who still bears latent tendency, of a body possessed of consciousness. Outflow-possessing coarse-heaviness: when the latent tendency is severed, the originally obtained nature, the unsettledness, the suffering-prone quality, and the similarly incapacitated nature, arising from and habituated by outflow, all grow faint. This outflow-possessing coarse-heaviness is also called the habitual residue of affliction, which neither an arhat nor a solitary awakened one is able to sever; only the Tathāgata can sever it to its very end, and so this is called the uncommon Buddha-quality of permanently severing habitual residue. This is called establishing affliction defilement through five distinguishing characteristics.

items.zh: 問：如世尊言：妄分別貪名士夫欲。以何因緣，唯煩惱欲說名為欲，非事欲耶？答：以煩惱欲性染污故。又唯煩惱欲能欲事欲故。又煩惱欲發動事欲，令生種種雜染過患。

items.title: Section: Correlating Scripture — Why "Desire" Means the Craving, Not the Object

items.zh: 謂諸所有妄分別貪未斷未知故，先為欲愛之所燒惱；欲愛燒故，追求諸欲；追求欲故，便受種種身心疲苦。雖設功勞，若不稱遂，便謂我今唐捐其功，乃受劬勞無果之苦。設得稱遂，便深戀著，守掌因緣，受防護苦。若受用時，貪火所燒，於內便受不寂靜苦。若彼失壞，受愁憂苦。由隨念故，受追憶苦。又由是因，發起身語及意惡行。又出家者棄捨欲時，雖復捨離煩惱欲因，欲復還起。又唯煩惱欲因緣故，能招欲界生老病死惡趣等苦。如是等輩雜染過患，皆煩惱欲以為因緣，是故世尊唯煩惱欲說名為欲，非於事欲。
items.en: Because false discriminative craving is neither severed nor recognised, one is first scorched by the burning of desirous craving; burned by that craving, one pursues desired objects; pursuing them, one suffers various bodily and mental exhaustion. Though effort is expended, if it does not succeed as hoped, one thinks one's effort has been wasted, and suffers the pain of toil without fruit. If it does succeed as hoped, one becomes deeply attached, and guarding it, suffers the pain of protection. While enjoying it, burned by the fire of craving, one suffers inward unrest. When it is lost or destroyed, one suffers grief and sorrow. Through remembering it, one suffers the pain of recollection. And by this same cause, unwholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind is generated. Also, one who renounces the household and gives up its objects of desire although having given up the cause of affliction-desire, still finds desire arising again. And it is affliction-desire alone that brings about, in the desire realm, the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, death, and the evil destinies. All such defiled misfortunes have affliction-desire as their cause, and so the Blessed One spoke only of affliction-desire as desire, not of the desired object.

items.title: Section: Eight Kinds of Discrimination That Kindle Desire

items.zh: 問：能生欲貪虛妄分別，凡有幾種？答：略有八種。一、引發分別，二、覺悟分別，三、合結分別，四、有相分別，五、親昵分別，六、喜樂分別，七、侵逼分別，八、極親昵分別。如梵問經言：引發與覺悟，及餘和合結，有相若親昵，亦多種喜樂，侵逼極親昵，名虛妄分別；能生於欲貪，智者當遠離。引發分別者，謂捨善方便心相續已，於諸欲中發生作意。
items.en: Question: how many kinds of false discrimination give rise to desirous craving? Answer: in brief, there are eight. First, inducing discrimination. Second, awakening discrimination. Third, uniting-and-bonding discrimination. Fourth, marked discrimination. Fifth, intimate discrimination. Sixth, joyful discrimination. Seventh, encroaching discrimination. Eighth, utterly intimate discrimination. As the Brahma's Questions Sutra says: inducing and awakening, and the rest, uniting and bonding, being marked and intimate, and manifold joy, encroaching and utterly intimate — these are called false discrimination; they give rise to desirous craving, and the wise should keep far from them. Inducing discrimination is this: once the continuity of the mind's own skilful means has been abandoned, attention arises anew with respect to objects of desire.

items.zh: 覺悟分別者，謂於不和合不現前境，由貪欲纏之所纏縛。合結分別者，謂貪欲纏所纏縛故，追求諸欲。有相分別者，謂於和合現前境界，執取其相、執取隨好。親昵分別者，謂於和合現前境界，由貪欲纏之所纏縛。

items.title: Section: A Loquat's Whole Life Cycle — Completing the Eightfold Discrimination

items.zh: 喜樂分別者，謂由如是貪欲纏故，希求無量所受欲具。侵逼分別者，謂由一向見其功德，而受諸欲，倍更希求。極親昵分別者，謂為最極諸貪欲纏之所纏縛。問：何故欲界諸煩惱中，唯顯示貪以為欲相？答：若由是因，顯示貪愛為集諦相；即以此因，當知此相。問：何故顯示分別俱貪以為欲相？答：若此因緣令貪現前發起於貪，若此因緣受用事欲，總顯為一妄分別貪。又有一分棄捨諸欲而出家者，仍於諸欲起妄分別；為令了知虛妄分別亦是欲已，尋復棄捨，故顯分別亦是欲相。
items.en: Joyful discrimination is wishing, on account of this very entangling craving, for boundless objects of enjoyment. Encroaching discrimination is enjoying desired objects because one has come to see only their merits, and thereby wishing for redoubled enjoyment still further. Utterly intimate discrimination is being bound by the most extreme entangling craving of all. Also, some who have renounced desired objects and gone forth from the household life still generate false discrimination towards them; in order that they come to know that false discrimination is itself already desire, and thereupon abandon it, discrimination too is shown to be a mark of desire.

items.title: Section: Why Craving Alone Marks the Truth of Origination

items.zh: 問：何故唯說貪愛為集諦相？答：由二因緣。一者、貪愛是願不願所依處故；二者、貪愛遍生起故。所以者何？由彼貪愛於身財等所應期願，為現攝受故，便起期願。於非願處對治善中為非所願，現攝方便故，便起不願。由此願不願故，生死流轉無有斷絕。
items.en: Question: why is craving alone said to be the mark of the truth of origination? Answer: by two causes and conditions. First, craving is the basis of both wishing and not-wishing. Second, craving arises pervasively. Why is this so? Because that craving, with respect to body and possessions to be wished for, being presently enjoyed, gives rise to wishing. With respect to what is not wished, in the wholesome antidotes to it, through presently taking up their means of practice, it gives rise to not-wishing. Because of this wishing and not-wishing, the flow of birth and death continues without interruption.

blocks.text: What "desire" really means: not the things we want, but the wanting.

Master Cháng Bǎi: outflow-heaviness is the mind's incapacity from affliction; outflow-possessing heaviness is the body's incapacity with the residue of affliction. Ripened and corresponding results grow lighter.

The craving mind burns like fire, restless. Master Cháng Bǎi: though one gives up the objects of desire, the desire itself may not yet be given up. (Untranslated, 0625b26: why only affliction-desire is called desire, not the objects: it alone is defiled, it alone desires the objects, and it sets them in motion.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: they form a gradual deepening of craving, from shallow to deep; one withdraws from wholesome attention such as the contemplation of impurity. (Untranslated, 0625c23: definitions of four of them: craving towards absent objects, seeking them, grasping marks of present ones, and intimacy with them.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: lacking objects of desire does not mean being free of desire; if discrimination rooted in craving remains, desire remains.
Craving wished-for and unwished-for both increase affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: some, relying on craving for non-existence, do merit and absorption hoping not to be reborn.
"Lacking objects is not freedom from desire." Renunciation of things is a beginning; freedom is in the mind.

quiz.q: The English has "is what ... causes ... to grow faint." What is wrong with the subject and content?
options: these natures are the heaviness itself, growing faint; it is no agent; and 本所得性 is omitted
no problem: heaviness is a force weakening the others, so "causes" is right
the problem is "grow faint," which should be "vanish"
the problem is "outflow," which should be "leak"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the original natures are this life's ripened and corresponding results, and with the unsettledness, the suffering-prone nature, and similar incapacity, all grow lighter. Four natures are listed; the English omits the first and makes heaviness the cause of what is in fact its own lessening.

quiz.q: How do outflow-heaviness and outflow-possessing heaviness differ, and why is the latter called residue?
options: the former is mind's incapacity from affliction; the latter the body's and residue, unsevered by the two vehicles, an air of affliction
the former is bodily fatigue, remaining in arhats; the latter is seeds of the three poisons, severed by arhats
arhats have severed both
both are outsiders' terms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outflow-heaviness is the mind's incapacity from affliction, and outflow-possessing heaviness the body's incapacity with the residue of affliction; that atmosphere is not real affliction but has its air. This matches fascicle 57's point on residue and the Tathāgata.

quiz.q: Why did the Blessed One call only affliction-desire "desire," not the object?
options: because objects do not exist, all outer things being false, so that the treatise denies them and accepts only inner desire, a basic position unrelated to misfortunes
objects are all wholesome
monastics have no objects of desire
all defiled misfortunes have affliction-desire as their cause
quiz.why: The treatise gives this reason after listing the sufferings of pursuing, protecting, and losing. Master Cháng Bǎi: the craving mind burns like fire, restless; it brings the desire realm's birth, ageing, sickness, and death and the evil destinies. Objects are not denied; they just are not the cause.

quiz.q: The English has "has not thereby given up the very cause of affliction-desire." Which way does it go?
options: not reversed: renunciants give up nothing, 雖復 being a concession
it should read "has given up desire itself"
it should read "has never heard of desire"
reversed: the Chinese says the cause, household objects, has been given up, yet desire returns
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though the object of desire, the cause of affliction-desire, has been given up, affliction-desire has not been fully given up. The Chinese concedes the renunciation. The English says it has not been given up, reversing the concessive clause, although the conclusion is the same.

quiz.q: What is inducing discrimination, and what does the order of the eight show?
options: the first moment of eye-consciousness at beauty, unrelated to skilful means; the eight are parallel objects without order or depth, the sūtra merely listing them
attention to the Dharma; greed turning into hatred
attention in absorption; concentration turning into wisdom
after dropping the continuity of skilful means, attention to desire arises; desire deepens stage by stage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one withdraws from the skilful mind such as the contemplation of impurity, unable to keep it continuous; the eight are a gradual deepening of craving, from shallow to deep. So the list traces how desire grows, and the wise should keep far from it.

quiz.q: Why is discrimination shown as a mark of desire, and for whom?
options: for laypeople, since those without objects have no desire
for arhats
for renunciants still discriminating: lacking objects does not mean being free of desire
for outsiders
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha made this known to those monastics; lacking the objects of desire does not mean being free of desire; if discrimination based on craving remains, desire remains. The English "a mark of desire" is accurate.

quiz.q: Why is only craving said to mark the truth of origination?
options: craving is the heaviest unwholesome karma and only of the desire realm, so that the treatise, judging by weight and realm, calls it alone the cause
craving underlies wishing and not-wishing; craving arises pervasively
craving is hardest to sever and easiest to see
craving results from ignorance and causes ageing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: craving wished and craving unwished both increase affliction, and so the flow of birth and death never ends; craving pervades all feelings, all times, all objects. So even the wish not to exist is a form of craving, which explains why it alone marks origination.

quiz.q: The English has "being what is presently to be countered." Is 現攝方便 rendered rightly?
options: yes: 現攝 is what is now subdued, 方便 the method
no: it should be "skilful teaching"
no: it should be "present merit"
no: it means taking up means in this life, not being countered now
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in this life one practices various means, hoping not to be reborn in the three realms; relying on craving for non-existence one does merit and absorption, called wholesome antidotes. So 現攝方便 is about taking up means, not being countered. Even such practice still rests on craving.
